title: Composable stream adapters + client fallback patterns (PRD exploration)
content:
Purpose

Quick exploratory PRD for a lightweight set of primitives we can ship that make it easier for application developers to compose streamed responses with local fallback logic and small client adapters. The goal is not a full new protocol but a set of SDK patterns + minimal wire semantics that: (a) enable safe tool calls and structured frames, (b) let mobile/edge clients cope with partial output and intermittent connectivity, and (c) provide clear debugging signals for partial/merged responses.

Why this now

- We keep iterating on progressive/partial streaming SDKs but customers still reimplement similar fallback logic (local caching, re-request, simpler model variant).
- Mobile apps often block on full JSON frames and end up discarding partial output; leads to poor UX or brittle heuristics.
- Tooling and safety require a predictable place to intercept tool call frames so clients can gate or re-run side-effects.

Non-goals

- Not inventing another heavy streaming protocol. Prefer reuse of current hosted-api streaming envelope and small optional fields.
- Not replacing server-side rollouts, model routing, or the canonical function-calling surface. This is client-side ergonomics + thin wire hints.

Key ideas / primitives (high level)

1) Adapter hooks (SDK-level):
   - preframe: callback invoked when a new logical frame starts (metadata available). Good for UI scaffolding.
   - contentFrame: called as tokens/text/partial structured payloads arrive. SDK provides helpers to assemble candidate JSON or typed fragments.
   - terminalFrame: called on end-of-stream or explicit terminal flags.
   - errorFrame: called when frame-level parse errors, tool-call denials, or safety truncations occur.

2) Frame metadata (wire hint fields, optional):
   - frame_id (short string): unique per logical frame; used for resume and dedupe.
   - partial_kind (text|json|tool-call|attachment): helps SDK pick parser.
   - stable_seq (int): sequence number for reordering detection when multiplexing sessions.
   - confidence_hint (low|med|high): heuristic from server about the reliability of the structured parse (useful when server-side postprocessing is approximate).

3) Minimal structured framing for tool-calls:
   - Two-phase tool-call frame:
       * frame:tool-call:start {tool_id, call_id, args_summary}
       * frame:tool-call:complete {call_id, outcome_summary, attachments?}
   - SDKs should expose a toolCallFilter hook: app can implement idempotency, preflight checks, or queue the action until user confirmation (mobile).

4) Adapter composition model:
   - Provide a library of small client adapters that can be stacked: e.g., ResumableCache -> LowBandwidthMode -> ToolCallGate -> JSONAssembler -> UIShim.
   - Each adapter implements the hook interface and can be inserted declaratively in the SDK client config.

Examples / usage sketches

- Mobile low-bandwidth flow (idea):
  config.adapters = [
    LowBandwidthMode({tokenBudget: 512}),
    JSONAssembler({max_fragments: 3}),
    ToolCallGate({promptUser: true})
  ]

  Behavior: LowBandwidthMode asks server for condensed/fidelity-reduced frames (we need a server-side hint support), JSONAssembler tries to salvage top-level keys from partial fragments, ToolCallGate pauses tool-call frames and surfaces them to the app for explicit user confirmation before SDK issues any side-effecting network call.

- Web progressive editor:
  - JSONAssembler emits partial object patches as they become parseable. UI applies patches with optimistic placeholders. If later frames contradict, SDK emits a reconciliation event with a small diff.

Safety and idempotency considerations

- Tool call gating must be conservative: default should always surface tool-call intents to app unless the customer's policy opts into auto-execute (enterprise only).
- Calls must include a server-provided call_id to allow dedupe across retries and resends.
- On resume after disconnection, SDK should query a server-side endpoint to reconcile call_id states rather than blindly re-issuing. Link: ENG-1189.

Debugging and observability hooks

- Telemetry fields per frame (optional): frame_latency_ms, parse_errors, assembled_size_bytes. SDK should surface these back via the Console when developer opts in.
- A lightweight `replay` mode in SDK: persist raw frames (configurable TTL) and allow developers to re-hydrate the original sequence for offline debugging or unit tests.

Server expectations (thin)

- The server should include optional frame metadata fields when server-side postprocessing produced them. Absence of fields should degrade gracefully (SDK falls back to token stream).
- A compact query param e.g. ?client_adapters=low_bandwidth,json_assembler can hint server to produce slightly different frames (condensed or enriched). This is advisory only.

Backward compatibility plan

- All fields optional: start with an opt-in beta for SDKs. No breaking changes to existing streaming API.
- Implement adapters on top of current streaming envelope; only introduce wire hint fields with vendor prefix (x-rd-frame-*) to avoid collisions.

Open design questions (to surface in design review)

- How to avoid explosion of server-side permutations if many client adapter hints exist? (Server might only honor a small curated set.)
- What is the canonical format for partial-json fragments? newline-delimited JSON fragments? JSON patch? A hybrid?
- UX for tool-call gating on desktop vs mobile — default policies and enterprise overrides.
- Privacy/security implications of persisting raw frames locally for replay. Need retention limits and encryption guidance.

Next steps / proposed milestones

1) Validation spike (2 weeks): build a prototype SDK adapter chain in the JS SDK that implements JSONAssembler + ToolCallGate. Hook to an internal streaming endpoint that emits simple x-rd-frame-* hints. Internal playtest with Editor and Mobile app.
2) Design review (1 week): gather eng + security + product feedback on wire hints and tool gating policy.
3) Beta (6 weeks): provide SDK beta builds, server opt-in (flagged), Console telemetry for frame-level events. Ship sample apps and a migration guide.

Notes to self / loose thoughts

- Keep adapter API minimal: 3-4 hooks max, developer ergonomics > completeness.
- Consider a small set of canonical adapters shipped in core SDK and a plugin API for community contributions.
- We should audit existing hosted-sdk code paths for where we can plumb frame metadata without large refactor.

Appendix: rough SDK hook surface (very draft)

function onPreframe(frameMeta) -> boolean|void  // return false to drop
function onContent(chunk, frameMeta) -> void
function onTerminal(frameMeta) -> void
function onError(errorFrame) -> void

We will iterate this doc after the validation spike.

---
Author notes: pushing this into Drive because it overlaps many streaming ideas but tends to focus on the client-side composability aspect which I've not seen called out cleanly in other PRDs. Will follow up with a short demo video and a small sample app repo link to include in linked_artifacts after the spike.
